Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Attached is Acme's proposed redline to Exhibit D (pricing schedule). The key commercial asks are:

- Remove the minimum monthly spend floor for the first 6 months and replace with a tiered variable-rate safety net tied to observed QPS/usage.
- Cap token/unit price increases to +12% per quarter; remove any unilateral repricing language.
- Introduce an automatic credit mechanism if latency/service objectives degrade >20% for a rolling 30-day period.

We tried to keep language operational rather than contractual where possible — see comments in the PDF. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the variable-rate safety net for the onboarding period; Acme needs this to match their forecasting model.

Folks — forwarding Acme's redlines. Quick thoughts before I respond to Jordan: 

- The floor removal for 6 months is doable if we keep a safety net that protects unit economics. I'm thinking a soft collar: a variable rate tied to committed-min usage but with a downside cap (e.g., no lower than 60% of list in months 1–3, 70% in months 4–6) instead of fully removing a floor.
- We should resist open-ended repricing limits that prevent us from making reasonable adjustments; a cap on increases (12%) seems fine if we preserve an indexation carve-out for infrastructure cost shocks.
- Credits for SLO degradation are reasonable but should be limited and tied to clear SLI thresholds and an incident review.

Requests: Rishi — can Legal draft a concise alternative collar language and two short fallback options (a) strict floor-with-credit, (b) soft-collar variable-rate with staged minimums?
Aditya — run a quick model on expected unit economics under the 60/70/100% staged floor vs Acme's proposed no-floor + safety net for 6 months.
Laura — if we accept the 12% cap on pricing increases, what does that mean for forecasted revenue over 12 months?

I want to propose a single counter that is simple and operational so procurement can sign quickly. cc'ing Rishi for legal language. I'll aim to reply to Acme by Friday EOD PST unless we need more time.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole

Marissa — see proposed compromise below (I've also attached a tracked PDF). High-level: accept a temporary variable-rate safety net for onboarding with a staged minimum (collar) and tightened credit language for SLOs.

Proposed points (concise):
1) Staged collar: Months 1–3: floor = 60% of agreed list unit price; Months 4–6: floor = 75%; Month 7 onward: standard contract floor applies (we revert to committed minimums in Order Form).
2) Variable-rate safety net: if observed usage is below the stated committed tier, Acme pays the floor amount (as above) OR we grant a one-time credit equal to 50% of the difference if shortfall is entirely due to documented integration delays.
3) Pricing increases: cap increases at 12% QoQ but allow an exception for verified infrastructure cost increases (public cloud compute index) with a 30-day notice and right for Acme to terminate if increase >20% cumulatively in 12 months.
4) SLO credits: credits capped at 10% of monthly invoice for any rolling 30-day window with >20% latency degradation; credits require joint incident RCA within 30 days and do not compound across multiple degraded metrics.

Attachment: ExhibitD_counter_redline_v2.pdf (contains tracked edits and short fallback clause (a) floor-with-credit and (b) soft-collar).

I kept the language modular so commercial can pick one option quickly. If you want, I can draft the short cover email to Acme summarizing the concessions and next steps for signature.

— Rishi Malhotra
VP, Legal | Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Attached is Redwood's counter (ExhibitD_counter_redline_v2.pdf) with a focused, operational compromise intended to keep onboarding predictable for Acme while protecting unit economics for Redwood. Highlights: 

- Temporary soft-collar for onboarding: Months 1–3 floor = 60% list; Months 4–6 floor = 75%; revert to standard Order Form minimums thereafter.
- Safety net flexibility: where shortfalls are due to documented integration delays, Acme may elect a one-time 50% credit on the difference in lieu of paying the full floor.
- Pricing adjustments: we will cap routine increases at 12% QoQ; we retain a narrow exception for verified infrastructure cost spikes (with 30 days notice).
- SLO credits: limited to 10% monthly, triggered by a documented >20% latency degradation for a rolling 30-day window and subject to joint RCA.

We believe this package addresses Acme's forecasting concerns while avoiding an open-ended permanent removal of minimums. If you agree in principle, we can convert Exhibit D and the accompanying order form to a DocuSign packet and route to your procurement team; we can also accept a single DocuSign execution of the Amendment + Order Form.

Next steps: please confirm (1) which fallback you prefer if integration delays apply (pay floor vs 50% credit), and (2) whether procurement wants a 6-month pilot clause added to the Order Form. If we get a yes on both, we'll issue the DocuSign link by Monday.

Attachments: ExhibitD_counter_redline_v2.pdf
